decisions.statement: The lualib pages are the index's answer for their page type in this checkout.
A page's code file takes the place of the scanned file named for the page's Lua export.
A scanned file no page names is taken from the scan unchanged.
A scanned file that is a page's own code file is taken from the page instead.
A build for Lua 5.0 takes a page's Lua 5.0 code where the page states that code.
A build for Lua 5.0 names the code each page's Lua 5.0 code is taken in place of.
An import naming the code of a page holding Lua 5.0 code names that page's feature.
A Lua export names its feature once the export's `__TS__` prefix is dropped.
A Lua export naming a feature outright names that feature.
A Lua export names its feature once the export's first letter is upper-cased.
A page naming no lualib feature either way refuses the build.
The refusal names the page's path and the name the page states.
A page's stated lua feature takes the place of the feature its Lua export names.
Two pages naming one lualib feature refuse the build.
That refusal names both pages' paths and the feature the two name.
A page whose code file is not there is passed over.
A page whose slug is no export name reads as nothing.
The code file of a page whose slug is no export name is named.
A page naming a feature the scan found nowhere is added after the scanned files.
The pages say how a source file's name reaches a feature name.
The pages say the name each source file's export is emitted under.
The name a page states is emitted whatever identifier that page's code exports.
A source file no page names is emitted under the name its own code exports.
A build for Lua 5.0 emits a page's Lua 5.0 code under the name that page states.
No page at all answers with the scanned files themselves.
Nothing here imports a page to read that page.

definition: the source file each lualib page names, in place of the file a tsconfig scan finds
